A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same color-correction research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original camera experiments on lightbox, in-the-wild, LSMI, and NUS data, together with simulation and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds calibration-point comparisons and additional estimated-white-point baseline results.

M1.justification: CST-MLP is renamed CCM-MLP. The chromaticity input, 32-unit hidden layer, eight predicted matrix entries, fixed central entry, cosine loss, noise augmentation, and multi-illuminant procedure remain unchanged. Newly specifying ReLU and the linear output layer documents implementation rather than establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same lightbox and in-the-wild data, single- and multi-illuminant LSMI scenes, and four NUS cameras. v4's main-text NUS section summarizes results already present in v3 Section S4 and Table S8; estimated-white-point testing also already existed.

E2.justification: v4 Section S1.3 adds evaluated 7-CCM and 7-RBF interpolation comparators. Table 3 also adds CCCNN and EXPINV, each with 1D and 2D inputs, to the CCMNet-estimated-white-point comparison previously reported without them in v3 Table S2. Other comparator sets remain unchanged after matching CST/CCM names.

E3.justification: Section S3.1 changes the reported Galaxy training/validation/test counts from 449/756/299 to 756/299/449, aligning them with the retained 50%/20%/30% description. This is a reported setting correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments. The new calibration ablation introduces seven LED calibration points with CCT or xy-RBF interpolation.

E4.justification: v4 adds a calibration-point ablation testing whether interpolation using seven off-locus LEDs provides an effective alternative to the learned mapping. Conversely, Table 2 removes the 3×19 polynomial and 3×13 root-polynomial ablations without retaining them elsewhere. Existing synthesis, LUT, noise, architecture, and metamerism analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean, percentile, and 10%-trimmed-mean reporting practices. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. Revised Table S2 statistics change results, not the estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Principal benchmark values remain unchanged, but all ΔE2000 entries in Table S2 are revised: for example, 2-CST/2-CCM mean error changes from 15.15 to 10.51, and the proposed 2D linear model from 13.37 to 10.88, reversing their ordering. v4 additionally reports 7-CCM/7-RBF angular errors of 28.29°/17.76°, new CCMNet-conditioned comparator scores, and removes two mapping-result rows. These are localized result revisions, not demonstrated same-setting model improvements.

T1.justification: The cosine-loss definition, image-synthesis derivation, multi-illuminant blending equations, and CCT estimation algorithm remain mathematically unchanged. Renaming transforms and explaining existing architecture do not introduce new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the 22% average LED-scene error reduction, backward compatibility, multi-illuminant support, and low computational cost; the introduction retains the same five contributions. The conclusion's more explicit LED-focused qualification is consistent with the near-Planckian caveat already documented in v3 Section S4.

C2.justification: v4 explains training-coverage gaps through the lightbox LEDs' limited chromaticity range and suggests broader LED coverage or synthesis as alternatives. It interprets the new calibration ablation as supporting learned 2D mapping and emphasizes applicability limits. However, its new claim that all methods benefit from 2D inputs under CCMNet estimates is contradicted by some Table 3 results.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies ReLU activation, a linear eight-neuron output layer, exact lightbox camera models, Chromaxion as the reflectance-data source, and color-chart masking during CCMNet estimation. It clarifies EXPINV's CCT conditioning and adds a project-page pointer advertised as providing code and data. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained implementations.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Chromaxion and Nair and Hinton's ReLU work. The substantive positioning against CCT interpolation and per-pixel neural color correction remains stable; other reference changes largely concern metadata, numbering, and placement.

P1.justification: v4 standardizes CCM terminology, makes localized explanatory edits, adds a main-text NUS subsection, and expands the robustness discussion. References move before the supplement, running headers are corrected, and author information and acknowledgements are updated. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 5 as a summary of existing Table S8 results, widens Table 3 with in-the-wild columns, and shortens Table 2. Figures 2–3 receive diagram-label refinements, several captions are shortened, table highlighting changes, and Figures 5–6 share a page. The underlying qualitative examples remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves reproducibility through explicit architecture and camera details, access information, and corrected Galaxy split reporting. Added calibration and robustness comparisons strengthen targeted validation, while the existing NUS findings become more visible. These gains outweigh limited losses from removing two ablation rows, but reporting remains imperfect: Table S2 revisions are unexplained, and the blanket 2D-benefit claim conflicts with CCCNN's new angular errors of 7.96° for 1D versus 10.77° for 2D in Table 3.
